Problem formulation. Let a patient be represented by a bag of frozen pathology foundation-model tile embeddings 𝐗 = { 𝐱 1 , … , 𝐱 N } , 𝐱 i ∈ ℝ D , \mathbf{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{x}_{N}\},\qquad\mathbf{x}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{D}, (1) where D = 1536 D=1536 for UNI2-h and D = 512 D=512 for CONCH. Let A , B ∈ { 0 , 1 } A,B\in\{0,1\} denote binary indicators for two molecular biomarkers. The corresponding molecular-state class index is defined as y s = 2 ​ A + B ∈ { 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 } . y_{s}=2A+B\in\{0,1,2,3\}. (2) The four biomarker configurations 00 00 , 01 01 , 10 10 , and 11 11 therefore correspond to class indices 0 0 , 1 1 , 2 2 , and 3 3 , respectively. State 00 00 denotes both biomarkers negative, 01 01 denotes biomarker B B positive only, 10 10 denotes biomarker A A positive only, and 11 11 denotes the joint-positive phenotype in which both biomarkers are positive. State 11 11 serves as the primary prediction target. For colorectal cancer, we define ( A , B ) = ( BRAF , MSI ) (A,B)=(\mathrm{BRAF},\mathrm{MSI}) , whereas for lung adenocarcinoma, ( A , B ) = ( EGFR , TP53 ) (A,B)=(\mathrm{EGFR},\mathrm{TP53}) . Figure 1 illustrates the biomarker-specific MIL branches, interaction module, and structured four-state prediction head. Biomarker-specific MIL representations. State-Aware Interaction MIL uses two separately parameterized gated-attention MIL branches [ 17 ] , each with its own tile projection and attention distribution, to produce biomarker-specific slide representations for the corresponding molecular targets. For biomarker k ∈ { A , B } k\in\{A,B\} , tile embeddings are projected to 256-dimensional features 𝐡 k , i ∈ ℝ 256 \mathbf{h}_{k,i}\in\mathbb{R}^{256} and assigned normalized gated-attention weights α k , i \alpha_{k,i} .

The corresponding slide-level representation is obtained as 𝐳 k = ∑ i = 1 N α k , i ​ 𝐡 k , i , ∑ i = 1 N α k , i = 1 , \mathbf{z}_{k}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\alpha_{k,i}\mathbf{h}_{k,i},\qquad\sum_{i=1}^{N}\alpha_{k,i}=1, (3) where the gated-attention module uses an attention dimension of 128. The two branch representations are therefore 𝐳 A = MIL A ( 𝐗 ) , 𝐳 B = MIL B ( 𝐗 ) , 𝐳 A , 𝐳 B ∈ ℝ 256 . \mathbf{z}_{A}=\mathrm{MIL}_{A}(\mathbf{X}),\qquad\mathbf{z}_{B}=\mathrm{MIL}_{B}(\mathbf{X}),\qquad\mathbf{z}_{A},\mathbf{z}_{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{256}. (4) Biomarker-specific linear classifiers map these representations to scalar logits, a = f A ​ ( 𝐳 A ) , b = f B ​ ( 𝐳 B ) . a=f_{A}(\mathbf{z}_{A}),\qquad b=f_{B}(\mathbf{z}_{B}). (5) Explicit biomarker interaction. Interactions between the biomarker-specific slide representations are modeled through the interaction vector 𝐮 = [ 𝐳 A , 𝐳 B , 𝐳 A ⊙ 𝐳 B , | 𝐳 A − 𝐳 B | ] ∈ ℝ 1024 . \mathbf{u}=\left[\mathbf{z}_{A},\,\mathbf{z}_{B},\,\mathbf{z}_{A}\odot\mathbf{z}_{B},\,|\mathbf{z}_{A}-\mathbf{z}_{B}|\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{1024}. (6) The interaction vector retains both biomarker-specific representations and augments them with their elementwise product and absolute difference. An interaction MLP g : ℝ 1024 → ℝ 256 → ℝ g:\mathbb{R}^{1024}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{256}\rightarrow\mathbb{R} (7) maps 𝐮 \mathbf{u} to a scalar interaction logit, i = g ⁡ ( 𝐮 ) . i=g(\mathbf{u}). (8) Structured four-state prediction. The four molecular-state logits are defined through a structured parameterization of the two biomarker-specific logits and their learned interaction: 𝐪 = [ q 00 , q 01 , q 10 , q 11 ] = [ 0 , b , a , a + b + i ] . \mathbf{q}=[q_{00},q_{01},q_{10},q_{11}]=[0,\;b,\;a,\;a+b+i]. (9) The double-negative state serves as the reference category and is assigned q 00 = 0 q_{00}=0 .

The two single-positive states are parameterized by their corresponding biomarker-specific logits, whereas the joint-positive state combines both biomarker-specific logits with the learned interaction term. When i = 0 i=0 , the joint-positive logit reduces to the additive combination of the two biomarker-specific logits, q 11 = a + b . q_{11}=a+b. (10) A nonzero i i allows the model to capture departures from the additive combination of the two biomarker-specific logits when estimating the joint molecular state. Molecular-state probabilities are obtained by 𝐩 = softmax ⁡ ( 𝐪 ) = [ p 00 , p 01 , p 10 , p 11 ] , \mathbf{p}=\operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{q})=[p_{00},p_{01},p_{10},p_{11}], (11) and the final joint-positive prediction is p joint = P ⁡ ( A = 1 , B = 1 ∣ 𝐗 ) = p 11 . p_{\mathrm{joint}}=P(A=1,B=1\mid\mathbf{X})=p_{11}. (12) Training objective. The model is trained using class-weighted cross-entropy over the four molecular states. For a patient with state label y s y_{s} , the state loss is ℒ state = − w y s ​ log ⁡ p y s , \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{state}}=-w_{y_{s}}\log p_{y_{s}}, (13) where the class weight for state c c is w c = N train 4 ​ N c . w_{c}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{train}}}{4N_{c}}. (14) Here, N train N_{\mathrm{train}} denotes the number of patients in the training partition and N c N_{c} denotes the number assigned to state c c . To provide direct biomarker-specific supervision to the two MIL branches, weighted binary cross-entropy losses ℒ A \mathcal{L}_{A} and ℒ B \mathcal{L}_{B} are applied to logits a a and b b , respectively. The corresponding positive-class weights are w A + = N A − N A + , w B + = N B − N B + , w_{A}^{+}=\frac{N_{A}^{-}}{N_{A}^{+}},\qquad w_{B}^{+}=\frac{N_{B}^{-}}{N_{B}^{+}}, (15) where N k + N_{k}^{+} and N k − N_{k}^{-} denote the numbers of positive and negative training patients for biomarker k k , respectively. The overall objective is ℒ = ℒ state + λ aux ​ ℒ A + ℒ B 2 , λ aux = 0.25 .

\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{state}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}\frac{\mathcal{L}_{A}+\mathcal{L}_{B}}{2},\qquad\lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}=0.25. (16) 3 Experimental Setup 3.1 Dataset and Labels State-Aware Interaction MIL and the comparison models are evaluated on two TCGA cohorts for distinct joint molecular phenotype prediction tasks. The colorectal cancer cohort comprises 443 patients from TCGA-COAD+READ [ 13 ] with both BRAF and MSI labels, and the lung adenocarcinoma cohort comprises 428 patients from TCGA-LUAD [ 14 ] with both EGFR and TP53 labels. Only patients with valid labels for both biomarkers and available foundation-model representations were retained. The primary prediction endpoint is the joint-positive phenotype, defined as BRAF + /MSI + in colorectal cancer and EGFR + /TP53 + in lung adenocarcinoma. Cohort composition and joint-positive prevalence are reported in Table 1 . Table 1: Cohort composition for joint molecular phenotype prediction. States 00 00 , 01 01 , 10 10 , and 11 11 denote the four biomarker configurations, with state 11 11 representing the joint-positive phenotype. Cohort Biomarker pair N N 00 00 01 01 10 10 11 11 Joint prevalence TCGA-COAD+READ BRAF/MSI 443 375 27 11 30 6.8% TCGA-LUAD EGFR/TP53 428 186 184 21 37 8.6% 3.2 Foundation Models and Baselines State-Aware Interaction MIL and all comparison models use frozen representations from UNI2-h [ 1 , 28 ] and CONCH [ 16 ] , which produce 1,536- and 512-dimensional tile embeddings, respectively. Whole-slide images are processed at 20 × 20\times magnification ( 0.5 ​ μ ​ m 0.5~\mu\mathrm{m} /pixel), with tissue regions identified using Otsu thresholding [ 6 ] and divided into 224 × 224 224\times 224 -pixel tiles. During training, up to 3,000 tissue tiles are randomly sampled per patient, while all available tile embeddings are used for validation and testing.

DirectJoint uses a single gated-attention MIL model [ 17 ] to distinguish the joint-positive phenotype from the remaining molecular configurations. IndependentPair trains two separate biomarker-specific MIL models and derives the joint prediction as the product of their marginal probabilities. NaiveMTL uses a shared gated-attention slide representation with separate prediction heads for biomarker A A , biomarker B B , and the joint-positive endpoint, without explicitly modeling interactions between biomarker-specific representations. PostHoc-LR combines the logits of the independently trained biomarker models using logistic regression. FourState-ABMIL uses a single gated-attention MIL encoder followed by a four-class linear head trained on the 00/01/10/11 molecular states using the same class-weighted cross-entropy used for state supervision in State-Aware. 3.3 Metrics and Training Parameters Joint-positive prediction performance is evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and average precision (AP). Results are reported as mean ± \pm standard deviation across five patient-level outer folds stratified by the four-state molecular label. The TCGA-COAD+READ test folds contain 83–93 patients with 5–7 joint-positive cases, while the TCGA-LUAD test folds contain 85–86 patients with 7–8 joint-positive cases. Within each outer-training partition, 15% of patients are reserved for inner validation, with stratification based on the four-state molecular label. All neural network models are trained using AdamW [ 2 ] with a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} , weight decay of 10 − 5 10^{-5} , and dropout of 0.10 0.10 for a maximum of 30 epochs, with gradient accumulation over four patient bags. Checkpoints are selected by validation AP, with early stopping after six epochs without improvement.

For PostHoc-LR , biomarker logits are standardized using training-set statistics and combined with class-balanced logistic regression using C = 1.0 C=1.0 , the liblinear solver, and a maximum of 2,000 iterations. 3.1 Dataset and Labels State-Aware Interaction MIL and the comparison models are evaluated on two TCGA cohorts for distinct joint molecular phenotype prediction tasks. With UNI2-h, State-Aware Interaction MIL achieved AP values of 0.5566 0.5566 in TCGA-COAD+READ and 0.2784 0.2784 in TCGA-LUAD, compared with 0.5161 0.5161 for NaiveMTL and 0.2525 0.2525 for IndependentPair, corresponding to improvements of 0.0405 0.0405 and 0.0259 0.0259 , respectively. State-Aware AUROC was lower than NaiveMTL in TCGA-COAD+READ and PostHoc-LR in TCGA-LUAD. Table 2: Joint-positive molecular phenotype prediction for BRAF + /MSI + in TCGA-COAD+READ (prevalence 6.8%) and EGFR + /TP53 + in TCGA-LUAD (prevalence 8.6%) using UNI2-h and CONCH pathology foundation-model representations.

The joint-positive prevalence was 6.8% in TCGA-COAD+READ and 8.6% in TCGA-LUAD, corresponding to prevalence-based reference AP values of approximately 0.068 and 0.086, respectively. Across both foundation-model representations, State-Aware improved AP relative to the comparison methods in both cohorts, indicating that the AP improvement was not specific to a single pathology representation. The AUROC results differed by representation: State-Aware was below the leading comparison method in both UNI2-h experiments, while its AUROC was above the comparison methods in both CONCH experiments. The corresponding UNI2-h ROC and precision–recall curves are shown in Figure 2 . In TCGA-COAD+READ, the precision–recall curves differ more visibly among methods than the ROC curves, reflecting the differences in AP. In TCGA-LUAD, the ROC and precision–recall curves overlap across methods, and the precision–recall curves intersect. In TCGA-COAD+READ (joint-positive prevalence 6.8%), AP was 0.5566 versus 0.4965 with UNI2-h and 0.4410 versus 0.3859 with CONCH. In TCGA-LUAD (joint-positive prevalence 8.6%), AP was 0.2784 versus 0.2418 with UNI2-h and 0.1659 versus 0.1529 with CONCH. AUROC was also higher for State-Aware in all four comparisons. This comparison indicates that four-state supervision alone did not reproduce the performance of State-Aware.

The no-interaction variant sets i = 0 i=0 , the no-auxiliary variant sets λ aux = 0 \lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}=0 , and the binary-supervision variant replaces the four-state objective with binary joint-positive supervision while retaining the biomarker-specific auxiliary losses.

Replacing four-state supervision with binary joint-positive supervision reduced both AUROC and AP across both cohorts and both foundation-model representations, indicating that retaining molecular-state information during training improved joint-positive prediction. Removing the interaction module reduced AP in both TCGA-COAD+READ experiments and in TCGA-LUAD with UNI2-h, while the no-interaction variant achieved higher AP with CONCH in TCGA-LUAD. Removing auxiliary biomarker supervision reduced AP in both TCGA-COAD+READ experiments and with UNI2-h in TCGA-LUAD, while AP with CONCH in TCGA-LUAD changed little. Given joint-positive prevalences of 6.8% in TCGA-COAD+READ and 8.6% in TCGA-LUAD, AP provides a useful measure of precision–recall performance, with these prevalences providing reference levels for interpretation. Joint-positive prediction performance was lower in TCGA-LUAD than in TCGA-COAD+READ for all methods with both UNI2-h and CONCH representations. The four-state analysis showed different separation patterns across the two cohorts: BRAF + /MSI + scores differed from all three alternative states in TCGA-COAD+READ, whereas EGFR + /TP53 + scores overlapped with the EGFR-only state in TCGA-LUAD. The consistent reduction under binary supervision suggests that retaining the non-joint molecular configurations provides useful supervisory information beyond a binary joint endpoint. Binary joint prediction combines the double-negative and two single-positive configurations into a single negative class, whereas four-state supervision preserves these molecular distinctions during training. The four-state score analysis supports this interpretation because joint-positive prediction scores differed across the molecular configurations. The effects of interaction modeling and auxiliary biomarker supervision varied across cohorts and foundation-model representations: both improved AP in the two TCGA-COAD+READ experiments and with UNI2-h in TCGA-LUAD, whereas with CONCH in TCGA-LUAD, removing the interaction module increased AP and removing auxiliary supervision produced little change.

The attention analysis shows that the prediction formulation can affect the spatial distribution of model attention in addition to the final slide-level prediction. Biomarker-specific representations and their interaction may influence which tissue regions receive greater attention during joint phenotype prediction. Limitations. The evaluation is limited to retrospective TCGA cohorts and does not include independent external validation across institutions or patient populations. The experiments are restricted to two cancer–biomarker pairs and two frozen pathology foundation-model representations. The limited number of joint-positive cases within individual test folds contributes to variability in the performance estimates. 6 Conclusion We presented State-Aware Interaction MIL for rare joint molecular phenotype prediction from whole-slide histology. The method preserves biomarker-specific representations, models their interaction, and supervises the complete four-state molecular configuration. Across TCGA-COAD+READ (6.8% joint-positive) and TCGA-LUAD (8.6% joint-positive), State-Aware improved AP with both UNI2-h and CONCH representations, while improvement in AUROC was observed with CONCH. The ablation experiments showed that retaining the complete molecular configuration during training improved joint-positive prediction, while the four-state analysis showed that prediction scores differed across molecular states.
These results support structured molecular-state supervision for predicting rare co-occurring biomarker phenotypes from pathology foundation-model representations.
